newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain welcomes Qatar's decision to return plane.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain welcomes Qatar's decision to return plane.

text.p: Bahrain on Tuesday welcomed Qatar's decision to return a helicopter used by a Bahraini air force pilot to defect to Qatar, but urged Doha to return the defector.
"Bahrain welcomes Qatar's decision to return the Bahraini transport military plane," Cabinet and Information Minister Mohammad Ibrahim al-Mutawae said in a statement.
Mutawae urged Qatar to return the pilot to Bahrain as soon as possible.
"The pilot was not banned from going to Qatar or any other country at any time... But his mistake was in the way he had chosen to go to Qatar," Mutawae said.
Qatar said on Tuesday it would return the helicopter to Bahrain but said the defector would be free to stay or go where he chooses,

"(Qatar's) foreign ministry explained to Bahrain's foreign ministry in an official memorandum that it had decided to return the military aircraft," the official source was quoted by Qatar's state-run news agency QNA as saying.
"The pilot will be free to stay in Qatar...return to his country or proceed to any other destination he might choose," the official said, adding the man could regard Qatar as his "second homeland".
Qatar on Monday said Bahraini air force pilot First Lieutenant Nasser Majed Nasser al-Khalifa had requested asylum after flying his helicopter to the capital Doha.
It was not immediately clear if the pilot belonged to Bahrain's al-Khalifa ruling family.

The apparent defection came as tensions between the two Gulf Arab states seemed to be easing after Bahrain's Emir Sheikh Isa bin Sulman al-Khalifa pardoned two Qatari sentenced to three years in jail in Manama for spying.
Bahrain and Qatar are locked in a dispute over small islands in the Gulf controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s but also claimed by Qatar.
Qatar has taken the case to the International Court of Justice in The Hague, angering Bahrain which, prefers Arab mediation.
